facts.fact: INSA's Director General said the House of People's Representatives unanimously ratified Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Proclamation No. 1426/2026, which sets 18 obligations for owners of 12 critical sectors, and that institutions are to use a transition period to prepare for compliance, so it is passed and not yet shown in force; the document gives no ratification date, so the date is its publication date, 2026-08-07.

facts.fact: The Federal Negarit Gazette 32nd Year No. 41 carries Critical Infrastructure Cyber Security Protection Proclamation No. 1426/2026, done at Addis Ababa on 21 July 2026 and signed by the President, and its article 28 provides that it enters into force one year after publication, so it is passed and not yet in force (commencement July 2027).

facts.fact: Birr Metrics reports Yohanis Daniel faced an additional charge under Ethiopia's computer-crime law for recording and live-streaming an August 2024 flight incident on TikTok.

The Federal High Court found Meskerem Abera (Ethio Neqat founder) guilty on two counts under Computer Crime Proclamation No. 958/2016 over two YouTube programmes, per her lawyer to BBC Amharic; sentencing was set for 11 November 2024.
The Computer Crime Proclamation No. 958/2016 was applied in a conviction by the Federal High Court.

A Bahir Dar University Journal of Law article treats the 2016 Computer Crime Proclamation as Ethiopia's current cybercrime law, which it says significantly amended earlier offences, and describes a 2019 draft Computer Crime Proclamation as a further proposed reform.

note: The Computer Crime Proclamation is held as ETH-006.
